fixes.explanation: True. Paul says not to be “…encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery.” (Galatians 5:1). A yoke is the frame that hitches animals to a load, and slavery is the one he doesn't want them back under. Notice the words “once more.” He's warning about something that's out there waiting for them.

Paul really does say this. The verse reads, “…do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery.” (Galatians 5:1). He gives the warning right after saying Christ has set them free. So yes, it's true, and the warning is right there in the text.

Whoa, careful, friend, that one flips it! Paul says the opposite. “Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you.” (Galatians 5:8). Whatever is getting in the way of their running, the One who calls them isn't behind it.

False, and Paul isn't mumbling about it. “Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you.” (Galatians 5:8). Whatever got in the way of their running, the One who calls them isn't behind it. Good catch, baker!

The whole batch, just like he says. “A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough.” (Galatians 5:9). Little goes in, and it reaches all of it. I've stamped plenty of dough, and a little bit never stays in its own corner of the bowl.

Whoa, flip that one over, friend. Paul says the opposite. “The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.” (Galatians 5:10). Paul doesn't name him, but he doesn't let him off either. I think this is a heavy line, so I'll say it once and let it sit.

Nope, no promotions in this verse, friend. Troubling the Galatians doesn't land anybody a corner office. Paul says, “The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.” (Galatians 5:10). I think that's a heavy thing to say, so I'll leave it right there.

True. “For you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh.” (Galatians 5:13). Paul puts the warning right alongside the call to freedom. I think he wants them to use that freedom well. Right after, he says, “Rather, serve one another in love.”
Paul does give that warning. He says, “…do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh.” (Galatians 5:13). It comes right after he says they were called to freedom. So yes, it's true.

That's the one. Paul says, “The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree…” and then names it: “Love your neighbor as yourself.” (Galatians 5:14). One decree holds the whole thing. That's a lot packed into a short line, friend.

That's one of the commands in the law (Exodus 20:8), but it's not the one Paul picks here. He says, “The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree…” and then names “Love your neighbor as yourself.” (Galatians 5:14). That's his single decree.

That's a command in the law too (Exodus 20:12), but Paul doesn't pick it here. He says, “The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree…” and then names “Love your neighbor as yourself.” (Galatians 5:14). Neighbor love is the one he names.

Consumed is the word. “But if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out, or you will be consumed by one another.” (Galatians 5:15). Notice the if: Paul is talking about what could happen if they keep on biting and devouring one another. That's why he says to watch out.

Shamed is a good guess, but Paul says something stronger. “…watch out, or you will be consumed by one another.” (Galatians 5:15). His warning is for if they keep on biting and devouring one another, friend. That's why he says to watch out.
